subject: Operator access limits & SCCs — EU-only processing Q&A
messages:
From: Marta Szymanski <marta.szymanski@odysseyhealth.eu>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Robert Fleming <robert.fleming@graystone-legal.co.uk>
Date: Wed, 27 Oct 2027 09:15:00 +0100
Subject: Questions on operator access limits for EU-only processing (SCCs)

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Odyssey Health is moving quickly and our Security & Privacy team has a few follow-ups before we can approve a pilot. High-level asks: we need confirmation that (1) all inference processing for our tenant is restricted to EU regions, (2) any operator (Redwood employee or contractor) access to data is subject to documented, limited conditions under the SCCs, and (3) we can receive evidentiary artifacts showing deletion of backups on demand.

Robert (cc'd) will consolidate legal questions, but can you confirm what operator roles exist, what triggers operator access (e.g., incident vs maintenance), and whether Redwood will accept contractual limitations around scope of access in the SCC Annex?

Appreciate a quick summary and any evidence artifacts you can share.

Best,
Marta
Head of Cloud Security, Odyssey Health

Attachments: none

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marta Szymanski <marta.szymanski@odysseyhealth.eu>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 27 Oct 2027 15:05:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Questions on operator access limits for EU-only processing (SCCs)

Hi Marta — thanks, and great to meet you both. Short answers up front, followed by detail and artifacts attached.

Summary:
- EU-only processing: Redwood supports EU-only inference for Odyssey via region pinning and dedicated in-region capacity — control plane resides in a private control plane option for this deal.
- Operator roles & triggers: We have defined operator roles (Tier 1 Support, Ops Engineer, Incident Responder, Platform Admin). Operator access to tenant data is allowed only for a limited set of operational reasons (P1 incident, legal compulsion, customer-authorized remediation) and is granted via time‑boxed, auditable access tokens.
- SCCs and Annex: We can accept SCC Annex language that limits operator roles and documents the purposes. We will propose language for the Annex and provide an operator access matrix and evidence artifacts for deletion requests.

I've attached: redwood-operator-access-matrix-v1.pdf (maps roles to allowed activities) and an explanatory note on how we implement SCC controls. You'll find our audit log retention and access workflow described.

Next steps:
1) Robert — if you can share specific Annex text you need, we can review and propose edits.
2) Marta — we can schedule a technical walk‑through of the access controls and a demo of the deletion evidence workflow next week.

--
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: redwood-operator-access-matrix-v1.pdf, sccs-explanatory-note.odt

From: Robert Fleming <robert.fleming@graystone-legal.co.uk>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marta Szymanski <marta.szymanski@odysseyhealth.eu>
Date: Thu, 28 Oct 2027 08:22:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Questions on operator access limits for EU-only processing (SCCs)

Sofia / Lauren,

Thanks for the quick summary and attachments — useful. A few legal points we need Redwood to confirm in writing for the SCCs Annex and for Odyssey's internal review:
1) A clear list of operator roles that may be considered "accessors" under the SCCs and the specific purposes (incident response, debugging, migration).
2) Confirmation that operator accounts are subject to MFA, conditional access, and just-in-time (timeboxed) elevation.
3) Whether Redwood will agree to a contractual prohibition on exporting copies of Odyssey data out of EU regions except under documented legal compulsion and with prior notice where possible.
4) Details on backups: do you retain cross-region backups by default? If so, can those be disabled for a dedicated enclave?

Also, please confirm what evidence format Redwood can provide for deletion requests (audit log entry, snapshot id, retention purge job id). We will propose Annex language but need these confirmations to be explicit.

Regards,
Robert
Senior Counsel, Graystone Legal

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Robert Fleming <robert.fleming@graystone-legal.co.uk>, Marta Szymanski <marta.szymanski@odysseyhealth.eu>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Oct 2027 11:40:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Questions on operator access limits for EU-only processing (SCCs)

Robert / Marta — hi. I'll address the questions in order and add concrete artifacts we can commit to in the contract.

1) Operator roles: we will provide a numbered list in the Annex. At a high level: Platform Admin (config management, infra changes), Ops Engineer (scheduled maintenance, scaling), Incident Responder (P1/P2 troubleshooting), Support Analyst (non-sensitive handlebars, telemetry triage). Only Incident Responder and Ops Engineer may, under documented P1 scenarios, request scoped access to inference session metadata; full request/response payloads are not accessible except when customer explicitly enables a support bundle.

2) Authentication & JIT: all operator accounts require 2FA, SSO, and are gated by time‑boxed privileged access (JIT) with supervisor approval recorded in the audit log. We will include contractual language requiring JIT and supervisor sign-off for any privileged data access.

3) Data export prohibition: for dedicated EU-only deployments we will accept language prohibiting the export of customer data outside the EU unless compelled by law. In compelled cases we will notify Odyssey promptly and provide legal basis.

4) Backups: default hosted plans do include encrypted backups; however, for Dedicated/EU-only we will provision a customer-isolated backup policy with in-region backups only and the option to disable automated cross-region replication. We will document the backup lifecycle and offer deletion confirmation artifacts (job id + timestamp + signed receipt).

Evidence format: we can provide a signed deletion manifest (job id, object ids/prefixes, UTC timestamp, operator id, and audit log pointer) and a snapshot id where applicable.

We'll prepare redlined Annex language and a draft SOP for operator access that we can include as a schedule. Jonas — can you help with the technical wording for the deletion manifest?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Product Security

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marta Szymanski <marta.szymanski@odysseyhealth.eu>, Robert Fleming <robert.fleming@graystone-legal.co.uk>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 16:02:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Questions on operator access limits for EU-only processing (SCCs)

Hi Marta / Robert — quick technical note to support the contract language. Below is an example deletion manifest we will provide and the corresponding log entries you can expect in the audit stream.

initiated_by: system (customer API) or operator: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
object_prefixes_deleted: s3://odyssey-eu/tenants/odyssey-12345/session-outputs/2027/10/*

deleted_objects_count: 1,243

Audit log entries include: access_request_id, approver_id, justification, IP, ephemeral token id, and retention purge job id. All audit entries are retained in-region and can be exported to a customer-owned logging sink (Push to customer SIEM) on request.

We will also include a sample Annex clause in the shared Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/ODYSSEY/ops-access-matrix

If this aligns with what you need, we can turn the example manifest into a contract exhibit and include the operator role list as a controlled Annex.

Best,
Jonas
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
